sentences.text:
by,
 The Inspector of Police,
 North Police Station (Crime),
 Tiruppur District.

Criminal Revision Petition filed under Section 438 r/w 442 of
 Bnss, to call for the entire records relating to the order made in
 Crl.M.P.No.6883 of 2024, dated 14.10.2024 on the file of the Judicial
 Magistrate No.I, Tiruppur and set aside the same insofar as dismissing
 petition for the offences under Section 318(4) and 316(2).

For Petitioner : Ms.R.Hemalatha
 For Respondent : Mr.S.Udaya Kumar
 Government Advocate (Crl. Side)
 1/4
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

 Crl.
 Order

The revision challenges the order of the learned Judicial Magistrate No.I, Tiruppur, who has allowed the petitioners application in part and directed the respondent to register an F.I.R. for offence under Section 506(ii) and 294(b) of I.P.C.
2.The learned counsel for petitioner would submit that the complaint discloses the offence under Section 420 of I.P.C. and that the respondent therefore ought to have added the said offence in the F.I.R.
The learned Magistrate, however, found that the offence of cheating is not made out.

By on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191754058/
1
Court is of the view that there is no infirmity in the impugned order.
However, if the respondent during the course of investigation finds that any other offence is made out, it is open to them to file an alteration report and proceed in accordance with law.
4.With the above observation, the Criminal Revision Case is dismissed.
